therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: somatostatin receptor agonism / dopamine receptor agonism
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: pituitary tumor growth suppression and prolactin secretion inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPA) or cabergoline-resistant prolactinomas
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: tumor volume changes (NFPA) and prolactin level changes (prolactinoma) from baseline to 6 months

results.effect_size: Median tumor volume: pasireotide 3.8 cm³ (95% CI 3.46–4.58) vs cabergoline 29.35 cm³ (95% CI 2.55–51.93)
biomarker_changes: Prolactin level changes assessed in resistant prolactinoma cohort treated with pasireotide
Tumor volume measured by MRI at baseline and 6 months
subgroup_findings: NFPA patients randomized to pasireotide showed lower median tumor volume than cabergoline arm (p<0.05)
Resistant prolactinoma patients treated with pasireotide: dose escalation to 900 µg twice daily if prolactin not normalized at 4 weeks

dose_info.dose: pasireotide 900 µg s.c. (NFPA); pasireotide 600–900 µg s.c. (prolactinoma); cabergoline 3 mg/week (NFPA)
dose_info.dose_modifications: Prolactinoma patients started at 600 µg s.c. twice daily; escalated to 900 µg s.c. twice daily at 4 weeks if prolactin not normalized
